method: The display-RGB pass estimates and divides out the measured 3.7 Hz and 5.3 Hz rapid exposure components with shot-dependent amplitudes. It reduces horizontal row offsets, forms edge-preserving luminance and opponent-color guides, and aligns nearby frames within each shot using dense optical flow. Forward and backward agreement and local residuals limit neighboring contributions at moving edges and occlusions. Local noise estimates control how much detail returns from the aligned observations. Luminance-guided chroma filtering targets the sections with larger color blotches, a clipped-noise correction reduces the upward bias in near-black samples, and a bounded inverse blend reduces visible trailing contours on selected motion. The three protected windows are copied sample for sample. Source credit covers the excerpt adapted from Spring (2019), Blender Foundation, directed by Andy Goralczyk, CC BY 4.0.
color_contract: 8bit displayRGB, same candidate transform; no linear/mastering reinterpretation
limitations: Rapid motion and occlusion reduce the number of reliable neighboring observations. Some soft motion and faint doubled contours remain around the upward turn, and small texture in the darkest fog can be attenuated. The lighting and motion comparisons use the supplied media. Reference-based PSNR, motion and lighting scores were unavailable.
